title: Check RetroAchievements Hardcore before a long gaming session
summary: Confirm game recognition, the active mode and recorded achievement progress. Keep normal saves safe and follow the client’s restrictions.
heroAlt: Original achievement-session diagram with game recognition and active-mode checks before a finish flag

blocks.text: Back up saves before changing settings

Use an emulator and platform supported by RetroAchievements, your own supported disc image and a working account connection. Back up normal in-game saves before changing settings. This guide concerns RetroAchievements, which is separate from an application’s local achievement system. Menu locations depend on the emulator. Check its documentation for the correct achievement controls.

Start the game normally and open its achievement information. Check that the correct game and achievement set are recognized. An unsupported revision or modified disc image may run but fail recognition. Solve that problem before attempting achievements. Selecting Hardcore cannot supply an absent achievement set or identify an unsupported image.

Confirm that Hardcore is active in the running game, not just selected in settings. It restricts conveniences such as loading save states and using cheats. Follow any restart prompt before attempting achievements. Do not bypass restrictions or assume an older save state is an eligible starting point. Some older clients call Casual mode Softcore.

If suitable, complete a short achievement you have not earned yet through normal gameplay. Confirm the unlock in the client and on the service. Check its recorded mode before beginning a long session. Switching modes afterward does not turn a Casual unlock into a Hardcore unlock. If a network or server error occurs, check synchronization rather than assuming it succeeded.
Practice separately and diagnose specific errors

For unrestricted practice, deliberately switch to Casual. Keep practice separate from a Hardcore attempt. If recognition or sign-in fails, retain your saves and investigate that specific error before reinstalling software. When requesting help, include the emulator version and game revision, but never publish account tokens or copyrighted game data. A normal in-game save remains useful for practice and recovery.
